RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — it's a weak contextual signal, common in senior public-sector recruitment and often explained by who holds the relevant senior roles. Raised on its own, it reads as an accusation and will put the ministry on the defensive.

Your stronger ground is procedural: you asked for written reasons two weeks ago and got nothing. In most civil services that reply is an obligation, with a deadline. Chase it formally, in writing, citing the relevant rule.

Then look at substance: your law degree plus public policy master's plus ten years versus a vaguer "international projects" claim. If the scoring criteria shifted or appeared late, that matters far more. Mention panel composition only as background, if at all.
